title: Plutonium Sample Half-Life Starter Activity from Backgrounder on Plutonium
learningObjectives: Explain that half-life is the time required for half of a radioactive sample to lose its radioactivity.
Compare how different plutonium isotopes decay at different rates and how shorter half-lives mean faster decay.
Use A = A0*(1/2)^(t/T) to predict the amount of a plutonium sample remaining after a given time.

explanations.text: Plutonium is a radioactive element that transforms as it decays. The half-life concept describes how quickly the amount decreases, which can be modeled with an exponential decay equation.

evidence.quote: Plutonium is a radioactive metallic element with the atomic number 94.
The different isotopes have different “half-lives” – the time it takes to lose half of its radioactivity.

explanations.text: Different plutonium isotopes have different half-lives. A comparison of two isotopes shows one decays much more slowly than the other, and materials with shorter half-lives decay more quickly.

evidence.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.
Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives, so they emit more energetic radioactivity.

explanations.text: As plutonium decays it changes into other isotopes or elements, many of which are still radioactive, illustrating why the remaining amount follows the half-life curve rather than disappearing instantly.

evidence.quote: Like any radioactive isotopes, plutonium isotopes transform when they decay.

predictions.prompt: A 100-gram plutonium-239 sample remains isolated for one half-life of 24,100 years. How much remains?
The same 100-gram plutonium-239 sample is measured again after a second half-life, 48,200 years total elapsed.
A 200-gram plutonium-241 sample with a 14.4-year half-life is stored for 28.8 years.
